text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like this, SPY and its analogs produced a median 5-session return of -0.1%, with outcomes ranging from -5.12% to 6.88%. The distribution is slightly right-skewed (skew 0.51) but leans negative more often than not: 52% of the analog sessions finished below zero. The single number to anchor on for path risk is the median max adverse excursion of -1.05%, which describes how bad the drawdown typically got during the week even when the final return was near flat.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs from 28 distinct sessions across 22 symbols because the current state combines three unusual features. First, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score is -1.985, meaning liquidity is historically thin. Second, WTI crude change over 20 days is 19.24%, a large energy shock. Third, 20-session realised volatility is only 9.16%, so the tape is quiet despite that oil move and low volume. Supporting features include a distance from the 52-week high of -2.27%, a 5d/20d volatility ratio of 1.192, a mean absolute overnight/weekend gap of 0.37%, and a drawdown from the 60-session peak of -1.84%. The feature weights allocate 30% to name-level price/volume, 20% to broad market, 20% to macro, 10% to crypto, and 20% to event timing, with 45 calendar days to the next earnings release. This specific mix of illiquidity, an oil spike, and compressed volatility pulls in other moments where markets were quietly digesting a commodity shock on thin volume.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the analog distribution has a mean of -0.03%, a standard deviation of 2.14%, a 10th percentile of -2.39%, a 25th percentile of -1.31%, a 75th percentile of 0.92%, and a 90th percentile of 3.29%. The worst outcome was -5.12% and the best was 6.88%. The histogram clusters heavily around the center, with 12% of episodes landing in the -0.37% bin and 14% in the 0.13% bin. The bad tail is populated by recent broad-market ETF sessions. The closest analog is IWM on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2997), which returned -2.98%. SPY itself on 2026-09-03 (distance 0.3101) returned -1.15%. DIA on 2026-09-02 (distance 0.3258) returned -1.86%, and JPM on 2026-09-04 (distance 0.3418) returned -2.37%. The positive tail includes SPY on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.3366), which returned 3.47%, and BAC on 2026-08-31 (distance 0.3223), which returned 1.24%. Seven of the 50 analogs are SPY itself, while 18 are broad ETFs.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still be difficult to hold through the week. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -1.05%. At the 25th percentile, the path dipped -1.98% intra-horizon, and at the 10th percentile it reached -3.1%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 0.99%, reaching 1.89% at the 75th percentile and 3.52% at the 90th percentile, yielding a reward-risk ratio of 0.94. In terms of drawdown breaches, 4% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown during the 5 sessions. Zero percent breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown.

[stress]
The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario worsens the baseline median by -4.51 percentage points, producing a median forward return of -4.61% and a 10th percentile of -11.63% across 48 analogs. The probability of breaching a 10% drawdown rises to 41.7%. Caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2025-04 tariff shock drops the median by -0.82 percentage points to -0.92% across 26 analogs, with a 10th percentile of -11.26% and a 23.1% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario shifts the median down by -1.99 percentage points to -2.09% across 50 analogs, with a 10th percentile of -5.01%. Caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare lowers the median by -0.99 percentage points to -1.09% across 50 analogs. Caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind produces a median of -0.49% across 36 analogs. Caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2023-03 regional bank stress actually improves the median by 1.51 percentage points to 1.41% across 36 analogs. Caveat: very short window; the analog set will be dominated by a handful of sessions. Among shock scenarios, the earnings release day drops the median by -0.69 percentage points to -0.79% across 50 analogs. Caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than the 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) shifts the median by -0.1 percentage points to -0.2%. Caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value. The liquidity air pocket moves the median by -0.03 percentage points to -0.13%. Caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not on a 7x24 venue; measured on the instrument itself, the reference market is closed for 81.4% of the week and 61.18% of its realised hourly movement happened in those closed hours. The FOMC decision day shifts the median by -0.01 percentage points to -0.11%. Caveat: only 92 decision days exist in the calendar, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. The policy-rate path re-pricing, crypto drawdown contagion, and China ADR de-rating scenarios all produce medians at or above the baseline. Caveats: rate re-pricing uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies and transmission depends on duration not captured here; crypto contagion uses BTC as a market-wide proxy without identifying name-level linkage; China ADR delisting risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space. No scenarios were skipped.

[limits]
The engine's own validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Out-of-sample conformal coverage is 80.8% against a target of 80%, but the matched coverage width is 10.2% versus 9.48% for the unconditional name benchmark, and the directional hit rate is 50.1%. The dataset spans 2513 sessions from 2016-09-20 to 2026-09-18 across 71 symbols. The wrapper status is "measured". For the primary Bitget SPY/USDT perpetual, the reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 61.18% of the wrapper's own realised hourly movement landed in those shut hours. It is classified as a "fair tracker" with a return correlation of 0.9477 and a tracking error of 23 bp/day. The basis band is -0.04% to 0.31%, and the spread is 0.13 bps. Caveat: a fair perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token; at 23 bp/day of tracking error it carries its own idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the basis band means the exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. Across 6 observed weekend blocks, the median weekend return was -0.101%, the 10th percentile was -0.506%, the standard deviation was 0.4191%, and the median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.2125%. Zero percent of those weekends breached a 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
